_comment: Roadmap VX11's cross-platform bitstream-hash gate - see tools/checks/check_cross_platform_hash.py for what this pins and why. Key: '<kernels-line-from-ac3cli--version>/<fast|reference>/<ac3|eac3|eac3_cpl>'. Value: SHA-256 of the matching file (gold.ac3/gold.ec3/gold_cpl.ec3) verify_gold_reference.sh's own encode step produces from tests/golden/audio/reference_51.wav. x86_64-sse2 and generic are measured directly (WSL2, GCC 16, real x86-64 hardware). aarch64-neon is measured on the REAL arm64 CI legs (PR #503, CI run 33635430769: linux-gcc-arm64, linux-llvm-arm64, windows-msvc-arm64, macos-llvm), not from the qemu cross-build this file previously declined to pre-fill from - and it comes back byte-identical to x86_64-sse2 on all three streams. That is the finding, not a formality: this project's ENCODER is bit-exact across architectures, so the ~6.02 dB gold-reference gap the arm64 legs measure is entirely decode-side. macOS x64 shares the x86_64-sse2 kernel and pins against it. Add any future leg's pin from its own CI run's 'unpinned' log lines.
